transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I get really scared right away if I think there might be a bat, or something flapping around in the stockroom. My heart kind of jumps, I start sweating, and I just feel like I need to get out of there immediately.
Does this intense fear happen only when you think there might be a bat or something flapping around?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean, I know a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I see something that looks like one, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway, my mind reacts like I’m in real danger.
Do you avoid the stockroom or back hallway because of this fear?

Yeah. I’ve been swapping out closing shifts when I can, and I’ll take the long way around the loading area just to avoid that back hallway. If I have to check the stairwell, I do it really fast, holding my phone, and I’m scared the whole time.
Have you ever had one of these sudden panic episodes when there was no bat, fluttering, or similar trigger around?
I don’t think so. It’s usually tied to seeing something or thinking there might be something flapping around. I can’t really remember it just coming out of nowhere.
